extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (PCT applicants/practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for preparing the description of a PCT international patent application, including required parts (title, technical field, background art, disclosure/summary, drawings description, best mode, industrial applicability), handling of deposited biological material, and requirements for nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings (WIPO ST.26/ST.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency (PCT Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The details required depend on national practice; draft with due regard to the practice of designated Offices (e.g., United States) to avoid amendments during national phase. A description complying with these provisions will be accepted by all designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention (Rule 5.1(a) / Administrative Instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall first state the title of the invention as appearing in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The heading 'Title of Invention' shall preferably precede the title. Follow the manner and order specified in Rule 5.1(a) unless a different order results in better understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Field (Rule 5.1(a)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the technical field to which the invention relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably precede this part with the heading 'Technical Field' (Administrative Instructions Section 204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Background Art (Rule 5.1(a)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the background art which, as far as known to the applicant, can be regarded as useful for the understanding, searching and examination of the invention, and, preferably, cite the documents reflecting such art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably use heading 'Background Art'. Citing documents reflecting the art is recommended to aid search and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure/Summary of Invention (Rule 5.1(a)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the invention, as claimed, in such terms that the technical problem (even if not expressly stated as such) and its solution can be understood, and state the advantageous effects, if any, of the invention with reference to the background art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably use heading 'Disclosure of Invention' or 'Summary of Invention'. Ensure the problem and solution are clear in relation to background art and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Description of Drawings (Rule 5.1(a)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the figures in the drawings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably use heading 'Brief Description of Drawings' and reference drawings where appropriate in examples and embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode / Modes for carrying out the invention (Rule 5.1(a)(v) and 37 CFR 1.435(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention claimed; this shall be done in terms of examples, where appropriate, and with reference to the drawings, if any. For international applications designating the United States the description must contain upon filing an indication of the best mode contemplated by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading examples: 'Best Mode for Carrying out the Invention', 'Mode(s) for Carrying out the Invention', or 'Description of Embodiments'. Where national law of a designated State does not require best mode, failure to describe the best mode shall have no effect in that State. Draft descriptions to satisfy the strictest designated Office if practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (Rule 5.1(a)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate explicitly, when it is not obvious, the way in which the invention is capable of exploitation in industry and the way in which it can be made and used, or, if it can only be used, the way in which it can be used; 'industry' is to be understood in its broadest sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably precede with heading 'Industrial Applicability'. Provide explicit statements about how the invention can be made/used to satisfy Offices requiring industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and headings of description parts (Rule 5.1(b),(c) and Administrative Instructions §204)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner and order specified (title, technical field, background art, disclosure, drawings description, best mode, industrial applicability) shall be followed except when a different manner/order results in better understanding and a more economic presentation. Each part should preferably be preceded by the appropriate heading suggested in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the suggested headings (e.g., 'Technical Field', 'Background Art', 'Disclosure of Invention', etc.). Deviate only when beneficial for clarity or economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to deposited biological material: required contents (PCT Rule 13 bis.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to deposited biological material shall indicate: (i) the name and the address of the depositary institution; (ii) the date of deposit; (iii) the accession number given by that institution; and (iv) any additional matter of which the International Bureau has been notified pursuant to Rule 13 bis.7(a)(i), provided the requirement was published in the Gazette at least two months before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such indications are not contained in the description they may be given on a separate sheet (preferably Form PCT/RO/134) and, if furnished at filing, attached to the request and referred to in the checklist. A reference made in accordance with PCT must be regarded by designated Offices as satisfying national law requirements on contents and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for furnishing references/indications for deposited biological material (Rule 13 bis.4 and 13 bis.3(a)/(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication not included in the application as filed may be furnished to the International Bureau within 16 months from the priority date and shall be considered by any designated Office to have been furnished in time if so; however, a designated Office may require earlier furnishing if it has notified the International Bureau and the requirement was published in the Gazette at least two months before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant requests early publication, any designated Office may consider indications not furnished before technical preparations for international publication have been completed as not having been furnished in time. The IB will notify applicant of receipt dates and will publish or forward dates/data depending on receipt timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and indications may be limited to certain designated States; different deposits allowed (Rule 13 bis.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to deposited biological material shall be considered made for all designated States unless expressly made for certain designated States only. References to different deposits of the biological material may be made for different designated States, and any designated Office may disregard a deposit made with an institution other than one notified by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Annex L of the PCT Applicant's Guide and the PCT Gazette to identify depositary institutions accepted by particular designated Offices. Make deposits with institutions notified by targeted Offices where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples of deposited biological material (Rule 13 bis.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: No furnishing of samples to third persons shall, except with the authorization of the applicant, take place before the expiration of the applicable time limits after which national processing may start; however, furnishing may occur if the applicant has entered national phase or certain national publication effects occur; national law governs furnishing thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities are not expected to request access, but may ask for samples only if they have notified IB and IB has published that notification (only Japan JPO has done so). If asked, the request is directed to the applicant who must arrange provision of samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: National notification and publication of requirements for deposited biological material (Rule 13 bis.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any national Office may notify the International Bureau of national requirements relating to references to deposited biological material (additional required matters or timing earlier than 16 months). Each national Office shall notify the IB of depositary institutions permitted under its law. The IB shall promptly publish such notifications in the PCT Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the PCT Gazette and Annex L of the PCT Applicant's Guide for country-specific requirements published by national Offices; ensure compliance when filing for those States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing inclusion requirement (PCT Rule 5.2 & AI Section 208)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application contains disclosure of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that are required to be included in a sequence listing, the description shall include a sequence listing part of the description complying with the standard provided for in the Administrative Instructions (Annex C / WIPO ST.26 or ST.25 as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must be presented as a separate part of the specification and comply with the applicable WIPO Standard (ST.26 for international filing dates on or after July 1, 2022; ST.25 for earlier filings). A single sequence listing compliant with WIPO ST.26 can be used across WIPO member state IPOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Standard ST.26 (post-July 1, 2022) format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that disclose nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences by enumeration must present each sequence and associated data in a standardized electronic XML format as a separate part of the specification, in accordance with WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is advisable to submit a ST.26-compliant sequence listing together with the international application on the international filing date rather than wait for an invitation from the ISA/IPEA. See MPEP §§ 2412-2419 for details and WIPO ST.26 resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and consequences for failure to furnish sequence listing (PCT Rule 13 ter.1 & 13 ter.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing complying with Administrative Instructions for purposes of international search, and may require payment of a late furnishing fee; if the applicant does not furnish the required listing and pay any required fee within the time limit, the ISA shall only be required to search to the extent a meaningful search can be carried out without the sequence listing. Any sequence listing not contained in the international application as filed shall not form part of the international application (but applicant may amend description under Article 34(2)(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper response to an ISA invitation includes submitting the sequence listing compliant with Annex C, paying any late fee (see 37 CFR references), and a statement that the listing does not go beyond the disclosure as filed. If not furnished, the ISA/IPEA's search/examination is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late furnishing fee for sequence listings (PCT Rule 13 ter.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The furnishing of a sequence listing in response to an invitation under paragraph (a) may be subjected by the International Searching Authority to the payment of a late furnishing fee whose amount shall be determined by the ISA but shall not exceed 25% of the international filing fee (excluding per-sheet fees for excess sheets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to pay a late furnishing fee if a compliant sequence listing is not provided with the international filing and the ISA issues an invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Offices cannot require non-standard sequence listings (PCT Rule 13 ter.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall require the applicant to furnish to it a sequence listing other than a sequence listing complying with the standard provided for in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings should comply with Annex C (AI). Use the standardized format to avoid differing national requirements; consult Annex L and the PCT Applicant's Guide for Office-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO-specific sequence listing submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an international application using the USPTO electronic filing system, the sequence listing part may be submitted as a single ASCII text file with a '.txt' extension or as a PDF file; 100 megabytes is the size limit for submitting a sequence listing text file via the USPTO system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission in PDF is not recommended because an ASCII/text electronic form is often required by ISA/IPEA for search/examination. If both PDF and ASCII are filed and the Request does not indicate which forms part of the application, the PDF will be considered part of the application and the ASCII only an accompanying item for search purposes.
